title.zh: 卷十三 梁書13: 列傳第三 朱瑄 朱瑾 時溥 王師範 劉知俊 楊崇本 蔣殷 張萬進
title.en: Volume 13 Book of Later Liang 13: Biographies 3 - Zhu Xuan, Zhu Jin, Shi Pu, Wang Shifan, Liu Zhijin, Yang Chongben, Jiang Yin, Zhang Wanjin
title.raw: 卷十三 梁書13: 列傳第三 朱瑄 朱瑾 時溥 王師範 劉知俊 楊崇本 蔣殷 張萬進 Volume 13 Book of Later Liang 13: Biographies 3 - Zhu Xuan, Zhu Jin, Shi Pu, Wang Shifan, Liu Zhijin, Yang Chongben, Jiang Yin, Zhang Wanjin

sentences.zh: 朱瑄，宋州下邑人也。

translations.literal: Zhu Xuan was a native of Xiayi in Song prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xuan came from Xiayi in Songzhou.

sentences.zh: 父慶，里之豪右，以攻剽販鹽為事，吏捕之伏法。

translations.literal: His father Qing was a local magnate who made his living by raiding and smuggling salt; officials seized him and he was executed by law.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qing, a village strongman, lived by banditry and salt-running until the authorities caught and executed him.

sentences.zh: 瑄坐父罪以笞免。

translations.literal: Xuan, implicated in his father's crime, was flogged and released.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan was caned and dismissed because of his father's offense.

sentences.zh: 因入王敬武軍為小校。

translations.literal: Thereupon he entered Wang Jingwu's army as a junior officer.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined Wang Jingwu's forces as a low-ranking officer.

sentences.zh: 唐中和二年，諫議大夫張浚征兵於青州，敬武遣將曹全晸率軍赴之，以瑄隸焉。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhonghe of Tang, Remonstrance Censor Zhang Jun raised troops at Qingzhou; Jingwu sent the general Cao Quanzhen with an army to join him, with Xuan attached to that force.
translations.idiomatic: In Tang Zhonghe year 2, Censor Zhang Jun mustered troops at Qingzhou; Jingwu dispatched Cao Quanzhen's army to answer the call, and Xuan went with it.

sentences.zh: 以戰功累遷列校。

translations.literal: Through battle merit he was repeatedly promoted among the column commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Repeated victories raised him through the ranks of field officers.

sentences.zh: 賊敗出關，全晸以本軍還鎮。

translations.literal: When the rebels were defeated and driven out of the passes, Quanzhen returned to garrison with his original army.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels broke and fled beyond the passes, Quanzhen marched his own troops back to their post.

sentences.zh: 會鄆帥薛崇卒，部將崔君預據城叛，全晸攻之，殺君預自為留後。

translations.literal: When Yan military commissioner Xue Chong died, his officer Cui Junyu seized the city in revolt; Quanzhen attacked, killed Junyu, and made himself acting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Yan commander Xue Chong died; his subordinate Cui Junyu rebelled and held the city. Quanzhen stormed it, killed Junyu, and declared himself acting commissioner.

sentences.zh: 瑄以功授濮州刺史、鄆州馬步軍都將。

translations.literal: Xuan, for merit, was appointed prefect of Pu and commander of Yan's horse-and-foot forces.
translations.idiomatic: For his service Xuan received Pu prefecture and command of Yanzhou's combined cavalry and infantry.

sentences.zh: 光啟初，魏博韓允中攻鄆，全晸為其所害。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangqi, Weibo's Han Yunzhong attacked Yan; Quanzhen was killed by him.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Guangqi reign Han Yunzhong of Weibo attacked Yan, and Quanzhen fell in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 瑄據城自固。

translations.literal: Xuan held the city and fortified himself.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan barricaded himself inside the city.

sentences.zh: 三軍推為留後。

translations.literal: The three armies pushed him to be acting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The army proclaimed him acting commissioner.

sentences.zh: 允中敗，朝廷以瑄為天平軍節度使，累加官至檢校太尉、同平章事。

translations.literal: When Yunzhong was defeated, the court made Xuan military commissioner of Tianping, and he rose in rank to honorary Grand Marshal and co-equal chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: After Yunzhong's defeat the throne appointed Xuan commissioner of Tianping; he eventually reached honorary Grand Marshal and co-equal chief minister.

sentences.zh: 太祖初鎮大梁，兵威未振，連歲為秦宗權所圍，士不解甲，危殆日數四。

translations.literal: When the Founder first held Daliang, his military prestige was not yet established; year after year he was besieged by Qin Zongquan, his men never doffing armor, peril coming several times a day.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder first governed Daliang his power was still weak; Qin Zongquan besieged him year after year, troops never out of mail, danger threatening several times daily.

sentences.zh: 太祖以瑄同宗，早兄事之，乃遣使求援於瑄。

translations.literal: The Founder, treating Xuan as a clansman, had long addressed him as elder brother, and sent envoys to seek aid from Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Calling Xuan kin, the Founder had long treated him as an elder brother and now begged him for help.

sentences.zh: 光啟末，宗權急攻大梁，瑄與弟瑾率兗、鄆之師來援，大敗蔡賊，解圍而遁。

translations.literal: At the end of Guangqi, Zongquan pressed the attack on Daliang; Xuan and his younger brother Jin led Yan and Yanzhou forces to the rescue, routed the Cai rebels, lifted the siege, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Guangqi, Zongquan hammered Daliang; Xuan and Jin marched troops from Yan and Yanzhou, crushed the Cai army, broke the siege, and retired.

sentences.zh: 太祖感其力，厚禮以歸之。

translations.literal: The Founder, grateful for their effort, sent them home with rich courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Grateful for the rescue, the Founder honored them lavishly on their departure.

sentences.zh: 先是，瑄、瑾駐於大梁，睹太祖軍士驍勇，私心愛之。

translations.literal: Earlier, while Xuan and Jin were encamped at Daliang, they saw the Founder's soldiers were fierce, and secretly admired them.
translations.idiomatic: While stationed at Daliang, Xuan and Jin had seen how fierce the Founder's troops were and coveted them.

sentences.zh: 及歸，厚懸金帛於界上以誘焉。

translations.literal: On returning home they hung out heavy rewards of gold and silk on the border to entice them.
translations.idiomatic: Back home they posted rich bounties of gold and silk along the frontier to lure deserters.

sentences.zh: 諸軍貪其厚利，私遁者甚眾。

translations.literal: The various armies, greedy for the rich profit, deserted in great numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Many of the Founder's men slipped away for the generous pay.

sentences.zh: 太祖移牒以讓之，瑄來詞不遜，由是始構隙焉。

translations.literal: The Founder sent a written protest; Xuan came with insolent words, and from this the rift began.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder rebuked him in writing; Xuan answered rudely, and enmity began.

sentences.zh: 及秦宗權敗，太祖移軍攻時溥於徐州。

translations.literal: When Qin Zongquan was defeated, the Founder shifted his army to attack Shi Pu at Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Zongquan's fall the Founder turned his armies on Shi Pu at Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 時瑄方右溥，乃遣使來告太祖曰：「巢、權繼為蛇虺，毒螫中原，與君把臂同盟，輔車相依。

translations.literal: At that time Xuan was backing Pu, and sent an envoy to tell the Founder: "Huang Chao and Zongquan in succession were vipers, poisoning the Central Plain; you and I clasped arms in alliance, cheek by jowl as in a chariot.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan was then siding with Pu and wrote the Founder: "Chao and Zongquan were serpents in turn, stinging the heartland; we clasped arms as allies, dependent as chariot wheels.

sentences.zh: 今賊已平殄，人粗聊生，吾弟宜念遠圖，不可自相魚肉。

translations.literal: Now the bandits are wiped out and people barely live again; my younger brother should think of the long view and not tear one another apart like fish and flesh."
translations.idiomatic: The rebels are gone and men barely survive; brother, keep the larger design—do not devour each other."

sentences.zh: 或行人之失辭，疆吏之逾法，可以理遣，未得便睽和好。

translations.literal: Perhaps a traveler's loose word or a border officer's excess may be settled by reason; you must not lightly break the good understanding."
translations.idiomatic: A courier's slip or a frontier officer's breach can be reasoned away; do not break our bond lightly."

sentences.zh: 投鼠忌器，弟幸思之。

translations.literal: When casting at a rat, one fears the vessel—brother, think on this."
translations.idiomatic: Strike the rat but spare the vessel—brother, weigh that."

sentences.zh: 」太祖方怒時溥通於孫儒，不從其言。

translations.literal: " The Founder was then angry that Pu was in league with Sun Ru and did not heed his words.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder, furious that Pu was colluding with Sun Ru, ignored the plea.

sentences.zh: 及龐師古攻徐州，瑄出師來援，太祖深銜之。

translations.literal: When Pang Shigu attacked Xuzhou, Xuan marched out to aid Pu; the Founder deeply resented it.
translations.idiomatic: When Pang Shigu besieged Xuzhou, Xuan came to Pu's aid, and the Founder never forgave it.

sentences.zh: 徐既平，太祖並兵以攻鄆，自景福元年冬遣朱友裕領軍渡濟，至乾寧三年宿軍齊、鄆間，大小凡數十戰，語在《太祖紀》中。

translations.literal: After Xu was pacified, the Founder united his forces to attack Yan; from winter of Jingfu year 1 he sent Zhu Youyu with an army across the Ji, until in Qianning year 3 he camped between Qi and Yan, fighting great and small battles several tens of times, as told in the 《Founder's Annals》.
translations.idiomatic: Once Xuzhou fell he massed troops against Yan: from winter of Jingfu 1 Zhu Youyu crossed the Ji, and by Qianning 3 armies lay between Qi and Yan in dozens of clashes recorded in the 《Founder's Annals》.

sentences.zh: 自是野無人耕，屬城悉為我有。

translations.literal: From then the countryside was untilled; all dependent prefectures became his.
translations.idiomatic: Fields lay empty; every subordinate city fell to him.

sentences.zh: 瑄乃遣人求救於太原，李克用遣其將李承嗣、史儼等援之。

translations.literal: Xuan then sent men to beg rescue from Taiyuan; Li Keyong dispatched his generals Li Chengsi, Shi Yan, and others to aid him.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan appealed to Taiyuan; Li Keyong sent Li Chengsi, Shi Yan, and other generals to help.

sentences.zh: 尋為羅宏信所扼，援路既絕，瑄、瑾竟敗。

translations.literal: Soon they were choked off by Luo Hongxin; the relief route cut, Xuan and Jin were defeated at last.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Hongxin soon blocked the road; aid failed, and Xuan and Jin were ruined.

sentences.zh: 乾寧四年正月，龐師古攻陷鄆州，遁至中都北，匿於民家，為其所箠，並妻榮氏擒之來獻，俱斬於汴橋下。

translations.literal: In the first month of Qianning year 4, Pang Shigu took Yanzhou; fleeing north of Zhongdu, hiding in a commoner's house, he was beaten by the household, and together with his wife Lady Rong was seized and presented; both were beheaded below Bian Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianning 4, month 1, Pang Shigu captured Yan. Xuan fled north of Zhongdu and hid in a peasant home; the family thrashed and seized him and Lady Rong, and both were executed at Bian Bridge.

sentences.zh: 朱瑾，瑄從父弟。

translations.literal: Zhu Jin was Xuan's younger cousin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Jin was Xuan's cousin.

sentences.zh: 雄武絕倫，性頗殘忍。

translations.literal: His martial valor was unmatched; his nature rather cruel.
translations.idiomatic: He was peerless in battle and notoriously harsh.

sentences.zh: 光啟中，瑾與兗州節度使齊克讓婚，瑾自鄆盛飾車服，私藏兵甲，以赴禮會。

translations.literal: In Guangqi, Jin was to marry Yanzhou military commissioner Qi Kerang; Jin came from Yan in splendid carriage and dress, secretly bearing arms and armor, to attend the wedding.
translations.idiomatic: During Guangqi Jin was betrothed to Qi Kerang of Yanzhou; he left Yan in lavish wedding gear with hidden weapons for the ceremony.

sentences.zh: 親迎之夜，甲士竊發，擄克讓，自稱留後。

translations.literal: On the night of fetching the bride, armored men sprang up secretly, seized Kerang, and Jin declared himself acting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On the wedding night his soldiers rose, kidnapped Kerang, and Jin proclaimed himself acting commissioner.

sentences.zh: 及蔡賊鴟張，瑾與太祖連衡，同討宗權，前後屢捷，以功正授兗州節度使。

translations.literal: When the Cai rebels ran wild, Jin allied with the Founder to attack Zongquan together; repeatedly victorious, for merit he was formally appointed Yanzhou military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: As Cai rebels spread, Jin joined the Founder against Zongquan, won battle after battle, and received formal appointment as Yanzhou commissioner.

sentences.zh: 既得士心，有兼並天下之意，太祖亦忌之。

translations.literal: Once he had won the soldiers' hearts, he harbored intent to swallow the realm; the Founder also feared him.
translations.idiomatic: He won the army's loyalty and dreamed of empire; the Founder feared him in turn.

sentences.zh: 瑾以厚利招誘太祖軍士，以為間諜。

translations.literal: Jin used rich rewards to entice the Founder's soldiers as spies.
translations.idiomatic: Jin bribed the Founder's men into spying for him.

sentences.zh: 及太祖攻鄆，瑾出師來援，累與太祖接戰。

translations.literal: When the Founder attacked Yan, Jin marched out to aid it and clashed with the Founder again and again.
translations.idiomatic: Each time the Founder struck Yan, Jin came to its defense and fought him repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 乾寧二年春，太祖令大將朱友恭攻瑾，掘塹柵以環之。

translations.literal: In spring of Qianning year 2, the Founder ordered the great general Zhu Yougong to attack Jin, digging trenches and palisades to ring the city.
translations.idiomatic: Spring of Qianning 2, the Founder sent Zhu Yougong against Jin with trenches and stockades encircling the city.

sentences.zh: 朱瑄遣將賀瑰及蕃將何懷寶赴援，為友恭所擒。

translations.literal: Zhu Xuan sent the generals He Gui and the foreign officer He Huaibao to the rescue; Yougong captured them.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan sent He Gui and the tribal general He Huaibao to relieve the siege; Yougong took them prisoner.

sentences.zh: 十一月，瑾從兄齊州刺史瓊以州降。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Jin's cousin Qi Qiong, prefect of Qi, surrendered the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In month 11 Jin's cousin Qi Qiong, prefect of Qi, surrendered his city.

sentences.zh: 太祖令執賀瑰、懷寶及瓊以徇於城下，語曰：「卿兄已敗，早宜效順。

translations.literal: The Founder had He Gui, Huaibao, and Qiong paraded below the wall, saying: "Your elder brother is already defeated; you should submit early."
translations.idiomatic: The Founder displayed He Gui, Huaibao, and Qiong before the walls: "Your brother is beaten—yield now."

sentences.zh: 」瑾偽遣牙將瑚兒持書幣送降，太祖自至延壽門外，與瑾交語。

translations.literal: Jin falsely sent the gate officer Hu'er with letter and gifts to surrender; the Founder himself came to the Yanshou Gate outside the wall to speak with Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Jin feigned surrender through Hu'er with gifts; the Founder met him at the Yanshou Gate.

sentences.zh: 瑾謂太祖曰：「欲令大將送符印，願得兄瓊來押領，所貴骨肉，盡布腹心也。

translations.literal: Jin told the Founder: "I wish to have a great general deliver the tally and seal; I beg my brother Qiong come to receive them, so that flesh and blood may lay open their hearts."
translations.idiomatic: "I will send a general with the seals," Jin said; "let my brother Qiong take them so kin may trust kin."

sentences.zh: 」太祖遣瓊與客將劉捍取符笥，瑾單馬立於橋上，揮手謂捍曰：「可令兄來，余有密款。

translations.literal: " The Founder sent Qiong with the guest officer Liu Han to fetch the tally box; Jin stood alone on horseback on the bridge, waved to Han and said: "Let my brother come—I have a private pledge."
translations.idiomatic: The Founder sent Qiong with Liu Han for the tally case. Jin waited alone on the bridge and called, "Send my brother—I have a secret to share."

sentences.zh: 」即令瓊往。

translations.literal: " He then ordered Qiong to advance.
translations.idiomatic: He had Qiong come forward.

sentences.zh: 瑾先令騎士董懷進伏於橋下，及瓊至，懷進突出，擒瓊而入，俄而斬瓊首投於城外，太祖乃班師。

translations.literal: Jin had first hidden the rider Dong Huaijin under the bridge; when Qiong arrived, Huaijin burst out, seized Qiong and dragged him inside, and soon beheaded Qiong and threw the head outside the wall; the Founder then withdrew his army.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Huaijin lay in ambush beneath the bridge, seized Qiong, dragged him in, and beheaded him; the head was thrown outside and the Founder marched away.

sentences.zh: 及鄆州陷，龐師古乘勝攻兗，瑾與李承嗣方出兵求芻粟於豐沛間，瑾之二子及大將康懷英、判官辛綰、小校閻寶以城降師古。

translations.literal: When Yanzhou fell, Pang Shigu pressed the attack on Yan; Jin and Li Chengsi were out foraging between Feng and Pei; Jin's two sons and the great generals Kang Huaiying, the aide Xin Tao, and the petty officer Yan Bao surrendered the city to Shigu.
translations.idiomatic: Yan fell and Shigu stormed Yanzhou while Jin and Li Chengsi foraged in Feng and Pei; Jin's sons, Kang Huaiying, Xin Tao, and Yan Bao handed the city to Shigu.

sentences.zh: 瑾無歸路，即與承嗣將麾下士將保沂州，刺史尹處賓拒關不納，乃保海州。

translations.literal: Jin had no road home; he and Chengsi led their followers intending to hold Yizhou, but prefect Yin Chubin shut the passes and would not admit them, so they held Haizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cut off, Jin and Chengsi aimed for Yizhou; Yin Chubin closed the gates, so they clung to Haizhou.

sentences.zh: 為師古所迫，遂擁州民渡淮依楊行密。

translations.literal: Pressed by Shigu, they then drove the prefecture's people across the Huai to rely on Yang Xingmi.
translations.idiomatic: Shigu drove them on until they fled across the Huai with their people to Yang Xingmi.

sentences.zh: 行密表瑾領徐州節度使。

translations.literal: Xingmi memorialized that Jin should hold the post of Xuzhou military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi had Jin appointed military commissioner of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 龐師古渡淮，行密令瑾率師以禦之，清口之敗，瑾有力焉。

translations.literal: When Pang Shigu crossed the Huai, Xingmi ordered Jin to lead troops against him; at the defeat of Qingkou, Jin contributed greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Shigu crossed the Huai; Xingmi sent Jin to meet him, and Jin was decisive at Qingkou.

sentences.zh: 自是瑾率淮軍連歲北寇徐、宿，大為東南之患。

translations.literal: From then Jin led Huai troops year after year raiding north into Xu and Su, a great scourge to the southeast.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Jin's Huai armies raided Xu and Su yearly and plagued the southeast.

sentences.zh: 及行密卒，子渭繼立，以徐溫子知訓為行軍副使，寵遇頗深。

translations.literal: When Xingmi died, his son Wei succeeded; he made Xu Wen's son Zhixun deputy commander of the campaign army, with deep favor.
translations.idiomatic: After Xingmi's death his son Wei ruled and favored Xu Wen's son Zhixun as deputy commander of the field army.

sentences.zh: 後楊溥僭號，知訓為樞密使，知政事，以瑾為同平章事，仍督親軍。

translations.literal: Later when Yang Pu usurped the title, Zhixun became commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and handled government affairs; Jin was made co-equal chief minister and still directed the personal guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Pu claimed kingship, Zhixun ran military affairs and government; Jin became co-equal chief minister and kept command of the guard.

sentences.zh: 時徐溫父子恃寵專政，慮瑾不附己。

translations.literal: At that time the Xu father and son, relying on favor, monopolized government, fearing Jin would not side with them.
translations.idiomatic: The Xu clan, arrogant in power, feared Jin would not obey them.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note:
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note:

sentences.zh: （陳彭年《江南別錄》云：徐知訓初學兵法於朱瑾，瑾悉心教之。

translations.literal: (Chen Pengnian's 《Separate Record of Jiangnan》 says: Xu Zhixun at first studied military arts under Zhu Jin; Jin taught him with all his heart.
translations.idiomatic: (Chen Pengnian's 《Separate Record of Jiangnan》 records that Zhixun first learned warfare from Jin, who taught him earnestly.

sentences.zh: 後與瑾有隙，夜遣壯士殺瑾，瑾手刃數人，埋於舍後。）〉

translations.literal: Later he had a rift with Jin and by night sent braves to kill Jin; Jin cut down several men with his own hand and was buried behind his quarters.)〉
translations.idiomatic: Later they quarreled; Zhixun sent killers by night and Jin slew several before he was buried behind his house.)〉

sentences.zh: 貞明四年六月，出瑾為淮寧軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of Zhenming year 4, Jin was transferred out to be military commissioner of Huaining.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenming 4, month 6, Jin was posted out as commissioner of Huaining.

sentences.zh: 知訓設家宴以餞瑾，瑾事之逾遜。

translations.literal: Zhixun gave a family feast to send Jin off; Jin served him with even greater deference.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixun held a farewell feast at home; Jin was more obsequious than ever.

sentences.zh: 翌日，詣知訓第謝，留門久之，知訓家僮私謂瑾曰：「政事相公此夕在白牡丹妓院，侍者無得往。

translations.literal: The next day he called at Zhixun's residence to thank him and waited long at the gate; Zhixun's household slaves privately told Jin: "The chief minister of government tonight is at the White Peony courtesan's house—attendants must not go."
translations.idiomatic: Next day he called to thank Zhixun and lingered at the gate; a servant whispered, "The chief minister is at the White Peony brothel tonight—no attendants allowed."

sentences.zh: 」瑾謂典謁曰：「吾不奈朝饑，且歸。

translations.literal: " Jin told the usher: "I cannot bear the morning hunger; I will return."
translations.idiomatic: "I am starving from the morning court," Jin said; "I am going home."

sentences.zh: 」既而知訓聞之，愕然曰：「晚當過瑾。

translations.literal: " When Zhixun heard it he said in alarm: "I should visit Jin this evening."
translations.idiomatic: Zhixun, startled, said he would call on Jin that night.

sentences.zh: 」瑾厚備供帳。

translations.literal: Jin lavishly prepared provisions and lodging.
translations.idiomatic: Jin laid out a rich feast and lodging.

sentences.zh: 瑾有所乘名馬，冬以錦帳貯之，夏以羅幬護之。

translations.literal: Jin had a famous horse; in winter it was stored in brocade curtains, in summer protected by gauze canopies.
translations.idiomatic: His prized horse slept under brocade in winter and gauze awnings in summer.

sentences.zh: 愛妓桃氏，有絕色，善歌舞。

translations.literal: His beloved concubine Lady Tao had supreme beauty and was skilled in song and dance.
translations.idiomatic: His favorite Tao was a peerless singer and dancer.

sentences.zh: 及知訓至，奉卮酒為壽，初以名馬奉，知訓喜而言曰：「相公出鎮，與吾暫別，離恨可知，願此盡歡。

translations.literal: When Zhixun arrived, Jin offered a cup of wine for long life; first he presented the famous horse; Zhixun said with pleasure: "The chief minister leaves his post for a time apart from me—parting sorrow is plain; let us drink our fill."
translations.idiomatic: Zhixun came; Jin toasted him and gave the horse. Zhixun said, "You leave office and leave me—our parting hurts; let us drink deep."

sentences.zh: 」瑾即延知訓於中堂，出桃氏，酒既醉，瑾斬知訓首，示其部下。

translations.literal: Jin then led Zhixun into the central hall, brought out Lady Tao, and when wine had muddled him, Jin cut off Zhixun's head and showed it to his troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the main hall he brought out Tao; when Zhixun was drunk Jin struck off his head and displayed it to the army.

sentences.zh: 因以其眾急趨衙城，知訓之黨已闔門矣，唯瑾得獨入，與衙兵戰。

translations.literal: Then with his men he rushed to the yamen city; Zhixun's faction had already shut the gates; only Jin entered alone and fought the yamen soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: He raced for the government compound; Zhixun's men had barred the gates—only Jin broke in and fought the guard.

sentences.zh: 復逾城而出，傷足，求馬不獲，遂自刎。

translations.literal: He climbed the wall again to get out, wounded in the foot, sought a horse and could not find one, and cut his own throat.
translations.idiomatic: He scaled the wall wounded, found no horse, and killed himself.

sentences.zh: 暴其屍於市，盛夏無蠅蛆，徐溫令投之於江，部人竊收葬之。

translations.literal: His corpse was exposed in the market; in midsummer no flies or maggots came; Xu Wen ordered it thrown into the river, but the people secretly recovered and buried it.
translations.idiomatic: His body lay in the market untouched by flies; Wen had it cast into the river, but townsfolk secretly buried it.

sentences.zh: 溫疾亟，夢瑾被髮引滿將射之。

translations.literal: When Wen fell gravely ill, he dreamed Jin, hair loose, drawing a full bow to shoot him.
translations.idiomatic: Wen, deathly ill, dreamed Jin with loose hair drawing a bow at him.

sentences.zh: 溫乃為之禮葬，立祠以祭之。

translations.literal: Wen then gave him a ceremonial burial and built a shrine to sacrifice to him.
translations.idiomatic: Wen buried him with rites and raised a shrine.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note:
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note:

sentences.zh: （馬令《南唐書》云：初，宿衛將李球、馬謙挾楊隆演登樓，取庫兵以誅知訓，陣於門橋。

translations.literal: (Ma Ling's 《History of Southern Tang》 says: At first the palace guards Li Qiu and Ma Qian seized Yang Longyan, climbed the tower, took arsenal weapons to execute Zhixun, and formed battle lines at the gate bridge.
translations.idiomatic: (Ma Ling's 《History of Southern Tang》 says guards Li Qiu and Ma Qian seized Longyan, armed from the storehouse to kill Zhixun, and formed ranks at the gate bridge.

sentences.zh: 知訓與戰，頻卻。

translations.literal: Zhixun fought them and was repeatedly driven back.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixun fought and was driven back again and again.

sentences.zh: 朱瑾適自外來，以一騎前視其陣，曰：「不足為也。

translations.literal: Zhu Jin happened to come from outside, rode forward alone to view their formation, and said: "They are not worth dealing with."
translations.idiomatic: Jin rode in from outside, scanned the line, and said, "This is nothing."

sentences.zh: 」因反顧一麾，外兵爭進，遂斬球、謙，亂兵皆潰。

translations.literal: Then he turned and waved once; the outer troops rushed in together, beheaded Qiu and Qian, and the disorderly soldiers all fled.
translations.idiomatic: He wheeled and signaled; outside troops poured in, killed Qiu and Qian, and the mob scattered.

sentences.zh: 瑾嘗有德於知訓者也，及其凶終，吳人皆謂曲在知訓。

translations.literal: Jin had once shown kindness to Zhixun; at his violent end, the Wu people all said the fault lay with Zhixun.
translations.idiomatic: Jin had once aided Zhixun; when he died violently, Wu opinion blamed Zhixun.

sentences.zh: 《五代史補》：瑾之奔淮南也，時行密方圖霸，其為禮待，有加於諸將數等。

translations.literal: 《Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties》: When Jin fled to Huainan, Xingmi was then planning hegemony and treated him with courtesy beyond other generals.
translations.idiomatic: The 《Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties》 notes that when Jin reached Huainan, Xingmi, planning supremacy, honored him above other commanders.

sentences.zh: 瑾感行密見知，欲立奇功為報，但憾無入陣馬，忽忽不樂。

translations.literal: Jin, moved by Xingmi's recognition, wished to repay with a striking deed, but regretted having no charger for the charge; he was restless and unhappy.
translations.idiomatic: Grateful for Xingmi's trust, he longed to repay with a brilliant victory but lacked a battle horse and brooded.

sentences.zh: 一日晝寢，夢老叟，眉發皓然，謂謹曰：「君長憾無入陣馬，今馬生矣！

translations.literal: One day at noon he napped and dreamed an old man, eyebrows and hair snow-white, who said to Jin: "You long regretted having no charger for the charge—now a horse is born!"
translations.idiomatic: At noon he dreamed a white-haired elder saying, "You lamented no war horse—now one is born!"

sentences.zh: 」及廄隸報，適退槽馬生一駒，見臥未能起。

translations.literal: " When the stable boy reported that a foal had just been born in the manger, he saw it lying unable to rise.
translations.idiomatic: The groom reported a foal just dropped in the stable, still unable to stand.

sentences.zh: 瑾驚曰：「何應之速也！

translations.literal: Jin said in alarm: "How swiftly it answered!"
translations.idiomatic: Jin exclaimed in alarm, "How fast the omen came!"

sentences.zh: 」行往視之，見骨目皆非常馬，大喜曰：「事辦矣！

translations.literal: Xing went to look; its bone and eyes were all unlike an ordinary horse; greatly pleased he said: "The affair is done!"
translations.idiomatic: He inspected it—bone and eye unlike any common horse—and cried in delight, "The affair is done!"

sentences.zh: 」其後破杜洪，取鍾傳，未嘗不得力焉。

translations.literal: Afterward in breaking Du Hong and taking Zhong Chuan he never failed to rely on its strength.
translations.idiomatic: Later, against Du Hong and Zhong Chuan, that horse never failed him.

sentences.zh: 初，瑾之來也，徐溫睹其英烈，深忌之，故瑾不敢預政。

translations.literal: At first, when Jin came, Xu Wen saw his heroism and deeply feared him, so Jin did not dare enter government.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin arrived, Xu Wen feared his brilliance and kept him from politics.

sentences.zh: 及行密死，子溥嗣位，溫與張鎬爭權，襲殺鎬，自是事無大小，皆決於溫。

translations.literal: When Xingmi died and his son Pu succeeded, Wen and Zhang Hao struggled for power; Wen ambushed and killed Hao, and from then matters great and small were all decided by Wen.
translations.idiomatic: After Xingmi's death Pu ruled; Wen killed rival Zhang Hao and thereafter decided everything.

sentences.zh: 既而溫復為自安之計，乃以子知訓自代，然後引兵出居金陵，實欲控製中外。

translations.literal: Then Wen, for his own security, placed his son Zhixun in his stead, and only then led troops out to dwell at Jinling, in truth intending to control inside and outside.
translations.idiomatic: Wen then installed Zhixun in his place and moved to Jinling with an army to rule court and provinces alike.

sentences.zh: 知訓尤恣橫，瑾居常嫉之。

translations.literal: Zhixun was especially overbearing; Jin constantly resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixun grew tyrannical; Jin hated him.

sentences.zh: 一旦知訓欲得瑾所乘馬，瑾怒，遂擊殺知訓，提其首請溥起兵誅溫。

translations.literal: One day when Zhixun wanted Jin's horse, Jin in anger struck and killed Zhixun, raised his head and begged Pu to raise troops to execute Wen.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhixun demanded his horse, Jin killed him, seized his head, and urged Pu to mobilize against Wen.

sentences.zh: 溥素怯懦，見之掩麵而走。

translations.literal: Pu was by nature timid; seeing it he covered his face and ran.
translations.idiomatic: Timid Pu covered his face and fled.

sentences.zh: 瑾曰：「老婢兒不足為計！

translations.literal: Jin said: "The old woman is not worth planning for!"
translations.idiomatic: Jin said, "That old crone is not worth a plan!"

sentences.zh: 」亦自殺，中外大駭且懼。

translations.literal: " He too killed himself; inside and outside were greatly alarmed and afraid.
translations.idiomatic: He too took his own life, and court and country panicked.

sentences.zh: 溫至，遽以瑾屍暴之市中。

translations.literal: When Wen arrived, he immediately exposed Jin's corpse in the market.
translations.idiomatic: Wen came and at once displayed Jin's body in the market.

sentences.zh: 時盛暑，肌肉累日不壞，至青蠅無敢輒泊。

translations.literal: It was high summer; the flesh for many days did not decay; even green flies did not dare alight.
translations.idiomatic: In midsummer the corpse did not rot for days; flies would not touch it.

sentences.zh: 人有病者，或於暴屍處取土煎而服之，無不愈。）〉

translations.literal: When people fell ill, some took earth from where the corpse was exposed, boiled it, and drank it—all were cured without exception.)〉
translations.idiomatic: The sick took soil from the exposed corpse, brewed it as medicine, and were invariably cured.)〉

sentences.zh: 時溥，徐州人，初為州之驍將。

translations.literal: Shi Pu was a man of Xuzhou; at first he was a fierce general of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Pu of Xuzhou began as one of the province's fiercest officers.

sentences.zh: 唐中和初，秦宗權據蔡州，侵寇鄰藩，節度使支詳命溥率師以討之，徐軍屢捷，軍情歸順，以節鉞授之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tang Zhonghe, Qin Zongquan held Caizhou and raided neighboring circuits; military commissioner Zhi Xiang ordered Pu to lead troops against him; Xu armies won repeatedly, the army's hearts turned to him, and the command seal was given him.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhonghe, Zongquan held Caizhou and harried the borders; Zhi Xiang sent Pu against him; Xu troops won again and again until the army chose Pu and gave him the commission.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note:
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note:

sentences.zh: （《舊唐書》列傳云：時溥，彭城人，徐之牙將。

translations.literal: (The 《Old Book of Tang》 biography says: Shi Pu, a man of Pengcheng, was a junior officer of Xu.
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Old Book of Tang》 calls Pu a Pengcheng man and a Xu staff officer.

sentences.zh: 黃巢據長安，詔征天下兵進討。

translations.literal: When Huang Chao held Chang'an, an edict summoned troops from all the realm to advance and attack.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang Chao seized Chang'an, the throne called the empire to arms.

sentences.zh: 中和二年，武寧軍節度使支詳遣溥與副將陳璠率師五千赴難，行至河陰，軍亂，剽河陰縣回。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhonghe, Wuning military commissioner Zhi Xiang sent Pu with deputy general Chen Fan to lead five thousand men to the rescue; reaching Heyin, the army mutinied and plundered Heyin county on the return.
translations.idiomatic: Zhonghe year 2, Zhi Xiang sent Pu and Chen Fan with five thousand men toward the capital; at Heyin the troops mutinied and looted the county on the march back.

sentences.zh: 溥招合撫諭，其眾復集，懼罪，屯於境上。

translations.literal: Pu gathered and comforted them; the masses reassembled; fearing guilt, they camped on the border.
translations.idiomatic: Pu rallied them, but fearing punishment they halted on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 詳遣人迎犒，悉恕之，溥乃移軍向徐州。

translations.literal: Xiang sent men to welcome them with rewards and fully pardoned them; Pu then shifted the army toward Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang sent envoys with gifts and a full pardon; Pu then marched on Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 既入，軍人大呼，推溥為留後。

translations.literal: Once inside, the soldiers shouted greatly and pushed Pu to be acting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Entering the city, the troops roared and made Pu acting commissioner.

sentences.zh: 送詳於大彭館。

translations.literal: They sent Xiang to the Great Peng lodge.
translations.idiomatic: They lodged Xiang at the Great Peng guesthouse.

sentences.zh: 溥大出資裝，遣陳璠援詳歸京。

translations.literal: Pu spent heavily from his stores and sent Chen Fan to escort Xiang back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Pu paid lavishly from his treasury and sent Chen Fan to escort Xiang to court.

sentences.zh: 詳宿七里亭，其夜為璠所殺，舉家屠害。

translations.literal: Xiang lodged at Qili Pavilion; that night Fan killed him, and the whole family was slaughtered.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang stopped at Qili Pavilion; that night Fan murdered him and butchered his household.

sentences.zh: 溥以璠為宿州刺史，竟以違命殺詳，溥誅璠，又令別將帥軍三千赴難京師。

translations.literal: Pu made Fan prefect of Su; because Fan had killed Xiang against orders, Pu executed Fan and ordered another general to lead three thousand men to the capital for the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Pu made Fan Su prefect, then executed him for killing Xiang; another general led three thousand men to aid the capital.

sentences.zh: 天子還宮，授之節鉞。

translations.literal: When the Son of Heaven returned to the palace, he granted Pu the command seal.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned to the palace, Pu received the commission.

sentences.zh: 及黃巢攻陳州，秦宗權據蔡州，與賊連結，徐、蔡相近，溥出師討之，軍鋒益盛，每戰屢捷。

translations.literal: When Huang Chao attacked Chenzhou, Qin Zongquan held Caizhou and linked with the bandits; Xu and Cai were near; Pu marched out to attack and his army's edge grew keener; in every battle he won repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: Chao besieged Chenzhou while Zongquan held Caizhou; Pu struck from nearby Xu and won battle after battle.

sentences.zh: 黃巢之敗也，其將尚讓以數千人降溥。

translations.literal: When Huang Chao was defeated, his general Shang Rang surrendered to Pu with several thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: After Chao's fall, his general Shang Rang surrendered several thousand men to Pu.

sentences.zh: 後林言又斬黃巢首歸徐州。

translations.literal: Later Lin Yan also sent Huang Chao's head to Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later Lin Yan delivered Chao's head to Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 時溥功居第一，詔授檢校太尉、中書令、钜鹿郡王。

translations.literal: At that time Pu's merit ranked first; an edict appointed him honorary Grand Marshal, Grand Secretary, and Prince of Julu.
translations.idiomatic: Pu's merit ranked first; the court made him honorary Grand Marshal, Grand Secretary, and Prince of Julu.

sentences.zh: 宗權未平，仍授溥徐州行營兵馬都統。

translations.literal: Zongquan not yet pacified, Pu was still appointed overall commander of Xu's campaign army and horse.
translations.idiomatic: While Zongquan still stood, Pu was named commander of Xu's field armies.

sentences.zh: 蔡賊平，朱全忠與之爭功，遂相嫌怨。

translations.literal: When the Cai rebels were pacified, Zhu Quanzhong disputed merit with him, and mutual resentment arose.
translations.idiomatic: After Cai fell, Zhu Quanzhong quarreled over credit and hatred grew.

sentences.zh: 淮南亂，朝廷以全忠遙領淮南節度，以平孫儒、行密之亂。

translations.literal: When Huainan fell into disorder, the court had Quanzhong hold Huainan military commission at a distance to pacify Sun Ru and Yang Xingmi's turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: Huainan rebelled; the court named Quanzhong distant commissioner to crush Sun Ru and Yang Xingmi.

sentences.zh: 汴人應援，路出徐方，溥阻之。

translations.literal: Bian men came to aid; the road passed through Xu territory; Pu blocked them.
translations.idiomatic: Bian troops marched through Xu; Pu barred the road.

sentences.zh: 全忠怒，出師攻徐。

translations.literal: Quanzhong was angry and sent troops to attack Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong attacked Xu in fury.

sentences.zh: 自光啟至大順，六七年間，汴軍四集，徐、泗三郡，民無耕稼，頻歲水災，人喪十六七。

translations.literal: From Guangqi to Datong, six or seven years, Bian armies gathered four times; in Xu, Si, and the three prefectures the people did not plow; years of flood followed; men lost six or seven in ten.
translations.idiomatic: For six or seven years Bian armies swarmed; Xu and Si lay untilled through flood and war until six or seven in ten were dead.

sentences.zh: 溥窘蹙，求和於汴，全忠曰：「移鎮則可。

translations.literal: Pu in straits sought peace with Bian; Quanzhong said: "Transfer your commission and it can be done."
translations.idiomatic: Desperate, Pu sued for peace; Quanzhong said, "Move your post and we may talk."

sentences.zh: 」朝廷以尚書劉崇望代溥，以溥為太子太師。

translations.literal: The court made Minister Liu Chongwang replace Pu, and made Pu Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent Liu Chongwang to replace Pu and made Pu Grand Preceptor of the Heir.

sentences.zh: 溥懼出城見害，不受代。

translations.literal: Pu feared leaving the city and being harmed, and did not accept replacement.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing murder if he left the walls, Pu refused to yield.

sentences.zh: 汴將龐師古陳兵於野，溥求援於兗州，朱瑾出兵救之；

translations.literal: Bian general Pang Shigu arrayed troops in the field; Pu sought aid from Yanzhou; Zhu Jin marched to rescue him;
translations.idiomatic: Pang Shigu camped in the open; Pu begged Yanzhou; Zhu Jin marched to his aid;

sentences.zh: 值大雪，糧盡而還。

translations.literal: Heavy snow fell; grain ran out and they returned.
translations.idiomatic: Snow blocked them; supplies failed and Jin turned back.

sentences.zh: 城中守陴者饑甚，加之疾疫，汴將王重師、牛存節夜乘梯而入，溥與妻子登樓自焚而卒，實景福二年也。

translations.literal: Those defending the walls were desperately hungry; plague added to it; Bian generals Wang Chongshi and Niu Cunjie entered by night on ladders; Pu and his wife and children ascended a tower and burned themselves to death—it was in fact Jingfu year 2.
translations.idiomatic: Defenders starved and sickened; Wang Chongshi and Niu Cunjie scaled the walls by night; Pu and his family burned themselves on a tower in Jingfu year 2.

sentences.zh: 地入於汴。）〉

translations.literal: The land passed to Bian.)〉
translations.idiomatic: Xu fell to Bian.)〉

sentences.zh: 王師範，青州人。

translations.literal: Wang Shifan was a man of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shifan came from Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 父敬武，初為平盧牙將。

translations.literal: His father Jingwu at first was a Pinglu junior officer.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jingwu began as a Pinglu staff officer.

sentences.zh: 唐廣明元年，無棣人洪霸郎合群盜於齊、棣間，節度使安師儒遣敬武討平之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tang Guangming, the Wudi man Hong Balang gathered bandits between Qi and Di; military commissioner An Shiru sent Jingwu to pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Guangming year 1, Hong Balang raided Qi and Di; An Shiru sent Jingwu to crush him.

sentences.zh: 及巢賊犯長安，諸藩擅易主帥，敬武乃逐師儒，自為留後。

translations.literal: When the Chao bandits invaded Chang'an, the various circuits arbitrarily changed their commanders; Jingwu then drove out Shiru and made himself acting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: As Chao ravaged Chang'an, circuits changed commanders at will; Jingwu expelled Shiru and seized the post.

sentences.zh: 王鐸承製授以節鉞，後以出師勤王功，加太尉、平章事。

translations.literal: Wang Duo by imperial order granted the command seal; later for merit in marching to aid the Son of Heaven he was raised to Grand Marshal and co-equal chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Duo invested him by imperial order; later aid to the throne won him Grand Marshal and co-equal chief minister.

sentences.zh: 龍紀中，敬武卒，師範年幼，三軍推之為帥，棣州刺史張蟾叛於師範，不受節度，朝廷乃以崔安潛為平盧帥，師範拒命。

translations.literal: In Longji, Jingwu died; Shifan was young; the three armies pushed him as commander; Di prefect Zhang Chan rebelled against Shifan and would not accept his command; the court then made Cui Anqian Pinglu commander, and Shifan refused the order.
translations.idiomatic: In Longji Jingwu died; the army made young Shifan commander; Di prefect Zhang Chan rebelled; the court named Cui Anqian commander and Shifan defied him.

sentences.zh: 張蟾迎安潛至郡，同討師範。

translations.literal: Zhang Chan welcomed Anqian to the prefecture and together attacked Shifan.
translations.idiomatic: Chan welcomed Anqian and jointly attacked Shifan.

sentences.zh: 師範遣將盧宏將兵攻蟾，宏復叛，與蟾通謀，偽旋軍將襲青州。

translations.literal: Shifan sent the general Lu Hong with troops to attack Chan; Hong rebelled again, conspired with Chan, and feigned a withdrawal to strike Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shifan sent Lu Hong against Chan; Hong turned traitor, plotted with Chan, and feigned retreat to strike Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 師範知之，遣重賂迎宏，謂之曰：「吾以先人之故，為軍府所推，年方幼少，未能幹事。

translations.literal: Shifan knew it; sent rich gifts to welcome Hong, and told him: "Because of my father's matter I am pushed by the military government; I am still young and cannot manage affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Shifan learned of it, welcomed Hong with gifts, and said, "The army made me commander because of my father; I am young and cannot rule.

sentences.zh: 如公以先人之故，令不乏祀，公之仁也。

translations.literal: If you, sir, because of my father's matter keep our sacrifices from failing, that is your benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: If you preserve our ancestral rites for my father's sake, that is mercy.

sentences.zh: 如以為難與成事，乞保首領，以守先人墳墓，亦惟命。

translations.literal: If you find it hard to succeed with me, I beg to keep my head and guard my ancestors' graves—that too is as you command."
translations.idiomatic: If you think me unfit, let me keep my head and tend the tombs—that is all I ask."

sentences.zh: 」宏以師範年幼，必無能為，不為之備。

translations.literal: Hong, because Shifan was young, was certain he could do nothing and made no preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Hong thought the boy helpless and took no precautions.

sentences.zh: 師範伏兵要路，迎而享之，預謂紀綱劉鄩曰：「翌日盧宏至，爾即斬之，酬爾以軍校。

translations.literal: Shifan set ambush on the road, welcomed and feasted him, and beforehand told the steward Liu Ye: "Tomorrow when Lu Hong arrives, you cut off his head; I will reward you with a field officer's post."
translations.idiomatic: Shifan ambushed the road, feasted Hong, and told Liu Ye, "When Hong comes tomorrow, strike off his head and I will make you a field officer."

sentences.zh: 」鄩如其言，斬宏於座上，及同亂者數人。

translations.literal: Ye did as told and beheaded Hong at table, and several co-rebels as well.
translations.idiomatic: Ye beheaded Hong at the feast and several conspirators with him.

sentences.zh: 因戒厲士眾，大行頒賞，與之誓約，自率之以攻棣州，擒張蟾，斬之。

translations.literal: Then he sternly warned the troops, gave great rewards, made oaths with them, personally led them to attack Di prefecture, seized Zhang Chan, and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: He rallied the army with rewards and oaths, led them against Di, captured Zhang Chan, and executed him.

sentences.zh: 安潛遁還長安。

translations.literal: Anqian fled back to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Anqian fled to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 師範雅好儒術，少負縱橫之學，故安民禁暴，各有方略，當時藩翰咸稱之。

translations.literal: Shifan elegantly loved Confucian learning, in youth bore horizontal-and-vertical arts, so in calming the people and forbidding violence he had measures each in place; the frontier governors of the time all praised him.
translations.idiomatic: He loved scholarship and stratagem, ruled with measured force, and frontier lords praised him.

sentences.zh: 及太祖平兗、鄆，遣朱友恭攻之，師範乞盟，遂與通好。

translations.literal: When the Founder pacified Yan and Yanzhou, he sent Zhu Yougong to attack him; Shifan begged alliance and then was on friendly terms.
translations.idiomatic: After the Founder took Yan, Yougong attacked; Shifan sued for peace and they allied.

sentences.zh: 天復元年冬，李茂貞劫遷車駕幸鳳翔，韓全誨矯詔加罪於太祖，令方鎮出師赴難。

translations.literal: In winter of Tianfu year 1, Li Maozhen seized and moved the imperial carriage to Fengxiang; Han Quanhui forged an edict adding crimes to the Founder and ordered the circuits to march troops to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Tianfu 1 winter, Maozhen seized the emperor at Fengxiang; Quanhui forged an edict condemning the Founder and summoned the circuits.

sentences.zh: 詔至青州，師範承詔泣下曰：「吾輩為天子藩籬，君父有難，略無奮力者，皆強兵自衛，縱賊如此，使上失守宗祧，危而不持，是誰之過，吾今日成敗以之！

translations.literal: When the edict reached Qingzhou, Shifan received it with tears and said: "We are the Son of Heaven's screen; the lord and father is in difficulty, yet none strives with force—all keep strong armies for themselves and let bandits go so far that the sovereign loses the altars of state; peril without support—whose fault is it? Today I stake success or failure on this!"
translations.idiomatic: The edict reached Qingzhou; Shifan wept and said, "We are the emperor's shield, yet none fights while the throne is lost—whose fault? Today I stake everything on this!"

sentences.zh: 」乃發使通楊行密，遣將劉鄩襲兗州，別將襲齊。

translations.literal: He then sent envoys to Yang Xingmi and dispatched Liu Ye to raid Yanzhou while another column struck Qi.
translations.idiomatic: He contacted Yang Xingmi, sent Liu Ye against Yanzhou, and struck Qi.

sentences.zh: 時太祖方圍鳳翔，師範遣將張居厚部輿夫二百，言有獻於太祖。

translations.literal: At that time the Founder was besieging Fengxiang; Shifan sent the general Zhang Juhou with two hundred cart bearers, saying there was tribute for the Founder.
translations.idiomatic: While the Founder besieged Fengxiang, Shifan sent Zhang Juhou with two hundred carts claiming tribute.

sentences.zh: 至華州城東，華將婁敬思疑其有異，剖輿視之，乃兵仗也。

translations.literal: Reaching east of Huazhou city, Hua general Lou Jingsi suspected something amiss, opened the carts and looked—inside were weapons.
translations.idiomatic: East of Huazhou, Lou Jingsi opened the carts and found weapons.

sentences.zh: 居厚等因呼，殺敬思，聚眾攻西城。

translations.literal: Juhou and the rest then shouted, killed Jingsi, gathered the masses, and attacked the west gate.
translations.idiomatic: They killed Jingsi, rallied men, and stormed the west gate.

sentences.zh: 時崔胤在華州，遣部下閉關拒之，遂遁去。

translations.literal: That day Cui Yin was at Huazhou; he sent subordinates to shut the passes and repel them, and they fled.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yin at Huazhou shut the gates and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 是日，劉鄩下兗州，河南數十郡同日發。

translations.literal: That day Liu Ye took Yanzhou; several tens of prefectures in Henan rose on the same day.
translations.idiomatic: That day Ye took Yanzhou; dozens of Henan prefectures rebelled together.

sentences.zh: 太祖怒，遣朱友寧率軍討之。

translations.literal: The Founder was angry and sent Zhu Youning with troops to attack.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder sent Zhu Youning to punish him.

sentences.zh: 既而友寧為青軍所敗，臨陣被擒，傳首於淮南。

translations.literal: Soon Youning was defeated by Qing troops, captured in battle, and his head was sent to Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Youning was defeated, captured, and his head sent to Huainan.

sentences.zh: 天復三年七月，太祖復令楊師厚進攻，屯於臨朐。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of Tianfu year 3, the Founder again ordered Yang Shihou to advance; he camped at Linqu.
translations.idiomatic: Tianfu 3, month 7, Yang Shihou advanced and camped at Linqu.

sentences.zh: 師厚屢敗青軍，遂進寨於城下。

translations.literal: Shihou repeatedly defeated Qing troops and then advanced his camp below the city.
translations.idiomatic: Shihou beat Qing armies repeatedly and pitched camp under the walls.

sentences.zh: 師範懼，乃令副使李嗣業詣師厚乞降，

translations.literal: Shifan in fear then ordered deputy envoy Li Siye to go to Shihou and beg surrender,
translations.idiomatic: Afraid, Shifan sent Li Siye to beg Shihou for terms,

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note:
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note:

sentences.zh: （《新唐書》云：師厚圍青州，敗師範兵於臨朐，執諸將，又獲其弟師克。

translations.literal: (The 《New Book of Tang》 says: Shihou besieged Qingzhou, defeated Shifan's army at Linqu, captured the generals, and also took his younger brother Shike.
translations.idiomatic: (The 《New Book of Tang》 says Shihou took Qingzhou, beat Shifan at Linqu, captured his generals and brother Shike.

sentences.zh: 是時師範眾尚十餘萬，諸將請決戰，而師範以弟故，乃請降。）〉

translations.literal: At that time Shifan's masses still numbered more than a hundred thousand; the generals asked for a decisive battle, but because of his brother Shifan requested surrender.)〉
translations.idiomatic: Shifan still had a hundred thousand men; his officers wanted battle, but for his brother's sake he surrendered.)〉

sentences.zh: 太祖許之。

translations.literal: The Founder permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder agreed.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，遣李振權典青州事，因令師範舉家徙汴。

translations.literal: After more than a year he sent Li Zhen to administer Qingzhou affairs provisionally and ordered Shifan to move his whole household to Bian.
translations.idiomatic: A year later Li Zhen governed Qingzhou while Shifan moved his family to Bian.

sentences.zh: 師範將至，縞素乘驢，請罪於太祖。

translations.literal: When Shifan was about to arrive, in white mourning he rode a donkey and asked forgiveness of the Founder.
translations.idiomatic: He came in white on a donkey to beg the Founder's pardon.

sentences.zh: 太祖以禮待之，尋表為河陽節度使。

translations.literal: The Founder treated him with courtesy and soon memorialized him as military commissioner of Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder honored him and soon made him commissioner of Heyang.

sentences.zh: 會韓建移鎮青州，太祖帳餞於郊，師範預焉。

translations.literal: When Han Jian was transferred to govern Qingzhou, the Founder feasted him in the suburbs; Shifan was present.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Jian took Qingzhou, the Founder feasted him outside the city; Shifan attended.

sentences.zh: 太祖謂建曰：「公頃在華陰，政事之暇，省覽經籍，此亦士君子之大務。

translations.literal: The Founder told Jian: "You, sir, formerly at Huayin in the leisure of government affairs read the classics—this too is a great task of gentlemen."
translations.idiomatic: The Founder told Jian, "At Huayin you read the classics in quiet hours—that is a gentleman's duty."

sentences.zh: 今之青土，政簡務暇，可復修華陰之故事。

translations.literal: Today Qing territory has simple government and leisure; you may again practice Huayin's old ways."
translations.idiomatic: Qing is quiet now; resume your Huayin studies."

sentences.zh: 」建撝謙而已。

translations.literal: Jian made modest disclaimers only.
translations.idiomatic: Jian demurred.

sentences.zh: 太祖又曰：「公讀書必須精意，勿錯用心。

translations.literal: The Founder also said: "When you read you must concentrate your mind—do not use it wrongly."
translations.idiomatic: The Founder added, "Read with care—do not misapply your mind."

sentences.zh: 」太祖以師範好儒，前以青州叛，故以此言譏之。

translations.literal: Because Shifan loved the Ruists, and earlier Qingzhou had rebelled, he spoke thus to mock him.
translations.idiomatic: He mocked Shifan's love of learning because Qing had rebelled.

sentences.zh: 及太祖即位，征為金吾上將軍。

translations.literal: When the Founder took the throne, he was summoned as General of the Golden Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder became emperor, Shifan was summoned as Golden Guard general.

sentences.zh: 開平初，太祖封諸子為王，友寧妻號訴於太祖曰：「陛下化家為國，人人皆得封崇。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiping, the Founder enfeoffed his sons as kings; Youning's wife cried out to the Founder: "Your Majesty has turned the family into a state; every man receives enfeoffment and honor.
translations.idiomatic: At Kaiping the Founder enfeoffed his sons; Youning's widow cried, "You ennoble everyone while my husband died because Shifan rebelled—what was his crime?"

sentences.zh: 妾夫早預艱難，粗立勞效，不幸師範反逆，亡夫橫屍疆場。

translations.literal: My husband early shared hardship and roughly established merit; unluckily Shifan rebelled, and my husband lay dead on the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: He served in hardship and died on the border when Shifan turned traitor.

sentences.zh: 冤仇尚在朝廷，受陛下恩澤，亡夫何罪！

translations.literal: The enemy still lives at court, receiving Your Majesty's grace—what crime had my husband!"
translations.idiomatic: The killer still enjoys your grace—what did my husband do wrong!"

sentences.zh: 」太祖淒然泣下曰：「幾忘此賊。

translations.literal: The Founder said tearfully: "I nearly forgot this bandit."
translations.idiomatic: The Founder wept, "I had nearly forgotten that villain."

sentences.zh: 」即遣人族師範於洛陽。

translations.literal: He immediately sent men to exterminate Shifan's clan at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He sent men to wipe out Shifan's clan at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 先掘坑於第側，乃告之，其弟師誨、兄師悅及兒侄二百口，鹹盡戮焉。

translations.literal: First they dug a pit beside the residence, then announced it; his younger brother Shihui, elder brother Shiyue, and sons and nephews two hundred mouths were all slaughtered.
translations.idiomatic: A pit was dug by his house; Shihui, Shiyue, and two hundred kin were slaughtered.

sentences.zh: 時使者宣詔訖，師範盛啟宴席，令昆仲子弟列座，謂使者曰：「死者人所不能免，況有罪乎！

translations.literal: When the envoy had read the edict, Shifan set a full banquet and seated brothers and nephews in order, telling the envoy: "Death is what no man can escape—how much more when guilty!"
translations.idiomatic: After the edict was read Shifan feasted his kin and told the envoy, "Death comes to all—especially the guilty."

sentences.zh: 然予懼坑屍於下，少長失序，恐有愧於先人。

translations.literal: Yet I fear being thrown into the pit below with young and old out of order—I would shame our ancestors."
translations.idiomatic: Yet I fear disorder in the pit and shame to our ancestors."

sentences.zh: 」行酒之次，令少長依次於坑所受戮，人士痛之。

translations.literal: As wine passed he had young and old go in turn to the pit to receive execution; gentlemen grieved for it.
translations.idiomatic: He had them drink by age and enter the pit in order; onlookers wept.

sentences.zh: 後唐同光三年三月，詔贈太尉。

translations.literal: In the third month of Later Tang Tongguang year 3, an edict posthumously made him Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Later Tang Tongguang 3, month 3, he was posthumously named Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 劉知俊，字希賢，徐州沛縣人也。

translations.literal: Liu Zhijun, style name Xixian, was a native of Pei county in Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhijun, courtesy name Xixian, came from Pei in Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 姿貌雄傑，倜儻有大志。

translations.literal: His bearing was heroic; he was unconventional and had great ambition.
translations.idiomatic: He looked heroic, was bold, and dreamed large.

sentences.zh: 始事徐帥時溥，為列校，溥甚器之，後以勇略見忌。

translations.literal: He first served Xu commander Shi Pu as a column officer; Pu greatly valued him, but later because of courage and stratagem was viewed with suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: He served Pu as a field officer, was favored, then feared for his prowess.

sentences.zh: 唐大順二年冬，率所部二千人來降，即署為軍校。

translations.literal: In winter of the second year of Tang Datong, he led his two thousand men to surrender and was appointed army officer.
translations.idiomatic: Datong 2 winter he defected with two thousand men and became an army officer.

sentences.zh: 知俊披甲上馬，輪劍入敵，勇冠諸將。

translations.literal: Zhijun donned armor, mounted, wheeled his sword into the enemy—his courage topped all generals.
translations.idiomatic: Armored on horseback he charged ahead of every general.

sentences.zh: 太祖命左右義勝兩軍隸之，尋用為左開道指揮使，故當時人謂之「劉開道」。

translations.literal: The Founder assigned the Righteous Victory and Victory armies to him; soon he was used as Left Vanguard commander, so people of the time called him "Liu Vanguard."
translations.idiomatic: The Founder gave him the Righteous Victory and Victory corps; he became Left Vanguard commander and was called "Liu Vanguard."

sentences.zh: 後討秦宗權及攻徐州，皆有功，尋補徐州馬步軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: Later in attacking Qin Zongquan and assaulting Xuzhou he had merit; soon he was made overall commander of Xu horse and foot.
translations.idiomatic: He fought Zongquan and took Xuzhou, then commanded Xu's horse and foot.

sentences.zh: 攻海州下之，遂奏授刺史。

translations.literal: In attacking Haizhou he took it and memorialized appointment as prefect.
translations.idiomatic: He captured Haizhou and was made its prefect.

sentences.zh: 天復初，曆典懷、鄭二州，從平青州，以功奏授同州節度使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianfu he successively governed Huai and Zheng; in pacifying Qingzhou, for merit he was memorialized military commissioner of Tong.
translations.idiomatic: Early Tianfu he held Huai and Zheng; pacifying Qing won him Tong commissioner.

sentences.zh: 天祐三年冬，以兵五千破岐軍六萬於美原。

translations.literal: In winter of Tianyou year 3, with five thousand troops he broke sixty thousand Qi troops at Meiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Tianyou 3 winter he routed sixty thousand Qi troops at Meiyuan with five thousand.

sentences.zh: 自是連克鄜、延等五州，乃加檢校太傅、平章事。

translations.literal: From then he took in succession Yan, Yan, and five other prefectures, and was raised to honorary Grand Tutor and co-equal chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: He then seized five prefectures including Yan and Yan and rose to honorary Grand Tutor and chief minister.

sentences.zh: 開平二年春三月，命為潞州行營招討使。

translations.literal: In the third month of spring of Kaiping year 2, he was ordered campaign commander of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Kaiping 2 spring, month 3, he was named Lu campaign commander.

sentences.zh: 知俊未至潞，夾寨已陷，晉人引軍方攻澤州，聞知俊至，乃退。

translations.literal: Zhijun had not yet reached Lu when the flanking camps had already fallen; Jin men led troops attacking Zezhou; hearing Zhijun had come, they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Before he reached Lu the camps had fallen; Jin besieged Zezhou but withdrew when he came.

sentences.zh: 尋改西路招討使。

translations.literal: Soon he was changed to western-route campaign commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made western-route campaign commander.

sentences.zh: 六月，大破岐軍於幕穀，俘斬千計，李茂貞僅以身免。

translations.literal: In the sixth month he greatly defeated Qi troops at Mugul, capturing and beheading a thousand-odd; Li Maozhen barely escaped with his body.
translations.idiomatic: Month 6 he crushed Qi at Mugul, killing thousands; Maozhen barely escaped.

sentences.zh: 三年五月，加檢校太尉、兼侍中，封大彭郡王。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of year 3 he was raised to honorary Grand Marshal and concurrent Palace Secretary, enfeoffed Prince of Dapeng.
translations.idiomatic: Year 3, month 5, he became honorary Grand Marshal, Palace Secretary, and Prince of Dapeng.

sentences.zh: 時知俊威望益隆，太祖雄猜日甚，會佑國軍節度使王重師無罪見誅，知俊居不自安，乃據同州叛，

translations.literal: At that time Zhijun's prestige daily grew; the Founder's suspicious nature daily deepened; when Youguo military commissioner Wang Chongshi was executed without crime, Zhijun could not rest easy in his place and then held Tong in rebellion,
translations.idiomatic: Zhijun's fame grew while the Founder grew suspicious; when innocent Wang Chongshi was killed, Zhijun rebelled at Tong,

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note:
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note:

sentences.zh: （《鑒戒錄》云：彭城王劉知俊鎮同州日，因築營牆，掘得一物，重八十餘斤，狀若油囊，召賓幕將校問之。

translations.literal: (The 《Mirror of Warning》 says: When Prince of Pengcheng Liu Zhijun was at Tong and built camp walls, he dug up an object weighing more than eighty jin, shaped like an oil bladder, and summoned guests and officers to ask about it.
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Mirror of Warning》 says that while fortifying Tong, Zhijun unearthed an eighty-jin object like an oil bladder and asked his staff.

sentences.zh: 劉源曰：「此是冤氣所結，古來囹圄之地或有焉。

translations.literal: Liu Yuan said: "This is grievance-qi congealed; in ancient prison grounds there sometimes is such."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuan said it was condensed grievance from an old prison site.

sentences.zh: 昔王充據洛陽，修河南府獄，亦獲此物。

translations.literal: Formerly when Wang Chong held Luoyang and repaired the Henan prefectural prison, this object was also obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chong had found the same when rebuilding Luoyang's jail.

sentences.zh: 源聞酒能忘憂，奠以醇醪，或可消釋耳。

translations.literal: Yuan heard wine can make one forget sorrow; offering pure wine might dissolve it.
translations.idiomatic: Wine might dissolve it, Yuan said.

sentences.zh: 然此物之出，亦非吉征也。

translations.literal: Yet the appearance of this object is also not an auspicious sign."
translations.idiomatic: Still, he added, the omen was ill.

sentences.zh: 」知俊命具酒饌祝酹，復瘞之。

translations.literal: Zhijun ordered wine and food prepared for libation, and reburied it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhijun poured wine, prayed, and reburied it.

sentences.zh: 尋有叛城背主之事。）〉

translations.literal: Soon there was the matter of rebelling and betraying the lord.)〉
translations.idiomatic: Soon he rebelled.)〉

sentences.zh: 送款於李茂貞。

translations.literal: He sent allegiance to Li Maozhen.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted to Li Maozhen.

sentences.zh: 又分兵以襲雍、華，雍州節度使劉捍被擒，送鳳翔害之，華州蔡敬思被傷獲免。

translations.literal: He also divided troops to strike Yong and Hua; Yong military commissioner Liu Han was captured and sent to Fengxiang to be killed; Hua's Cai Jingsi was wounded but escaped.
translations.idiomatic: He raided Yong and Hua; Liu Han was taken to Fengxiang and killed; Cai Jingsi was wounded but lived.

sentences.zh: 太祖聞知俊叛，遣近臣諭之曰：「朕待卿甚厚，何相負耶？

translations.literal: The Founder, hearing Zhijun had rebelled, sent a close attendant to instruct him: "I treated you very generously—why have you failed me?"
translations.idiomatic: The Founder asked, "I favored you—why betray me?"

sentences.zh: 」知俊報曰：「臣非背德，但畏死耳！

translations.literal: Zhijun replied: "Your subject does not betray virtue, but only fears death!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhijun answered, "I do not betray you—I fear death!"

sentences.zh: 王重師不負陛下，而致族滅！

translations.literal: Wang Chongshi did not fail Your Majesty, yet his clan was destroyed!"
translations.idiomatic: Chongshi was loyal, yet you wiped out his house!"

sentences.zh: 」太祖復遣使謂知俊曰：「朕不料卿為此。

translations.literal: The Founder again sent an envoy telling Zhijun: "I did not expect you would do this."
translations.idiomatic: The Founder said he never expected this of him.

sentences.zh: 昨重師得罪，蓋劉捍言陰結邠、鳳，終不為國家用。

translations.literal: Yesterday Chongshi's crime—because Liu Han said he secretly linked with Bin and Feng and in the end would not serve the state's use.
translations.idiomatic: Chongshi died because Han claimed he plotted with Bin and Feng and would never serve the throne.

sentences.zh: 我今雖知枉濫，悔不可追，致卿如斯，我心恨恨，蓋劉捍誤予事也，捍一死固未塞責。

translations.literal: Today though I know it was excessive punishment, regret cannot be undone; causing you to be like this, my heart hates it—the fault lies with Liu Han misleading me in the affair; Han's one death truly does not answer the blame."
translations.idiomatic: I know it was unjust and cannot undo it; Han misled me—his death is not enough."

sentences.zh: 」知俊不報，遂分兵以守潼關。

translations.literal: Zhijun did not reply and then divided troops to guard Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Zhijun was silent and garrisoned Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 太祖命劉鄩率兵進討，攻潼關，下之。

translations.literal: The Founder ordered Liu Ye to lead troops in pursuit, attacked Tong Pass, and took it.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder sent Liu Ye, who took Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 時知俊弟知浣為親衛指揮使，聞知俊叛，自洛奔至潼關，為鄩所擒，害之。

translations.literal: At that time Zhijun's younger brother Zhihuan was personal guard commander; hearing Zhijun had rebelled, he fled from Luo to Tong Pass, was seized by Ye, and killed.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Zhihuan fled from Luoyang to Tong Pass, was caught by Ye, and killed.

sentences.zh: 尋而王師繼至，知俊乃舉族奔於鳳翔；

translations.literal: Soon Wang's army followed; Zhijun then led his whole clan to flee to Fengxiang;
translations.idiomatic: Wang's army followed; Zhijun fled with his clan to Fengxiang;

sentences.zh: 李茂貞厚待之，偽加檢校太尉、兼中書令，以土疆不廣，無藩鎮以處之，但厚給俸祿而已。

translations.literal: Li Maozhen treated him generously, falsely raised him to honorary Grand Marshal and concurrent Grand Secretary; because territory was not broad there was no frontier post to place him in, but only rich salary was given.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhen honored him with empty titles but no domain, only rich pay.

sentences.zh: 尋命率兵攻圍靈武，且圖牧圉之地。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to lead troops to besiege Lingwu and also plan pasture lands.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent to besiege Lingwu and seize pasture.

sentences.zh: 靈武節度使韓遜遣使來告急，太祖令康懷英率師救之，師次邠州長城嶺，為知俊邀擊，懷英敗歸。

translations.literal: Lingwu military commissioner Han Xun sent an envoy in urgent appeal; the Founder ordered Kang Huaiying to lead troops to rescue; the army reached Changcheng Ridge in Bin prefecture and was intercepted by Zhijun; Huaiying was defeated and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Han Xun of Lingwu begged aid; Kang Huaiying marched, was ambushed at Changcheng Ridge, and retreated.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note:
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note:

sentences.zh: （《九國志》云：李彥琦、劉知俊自靈武班師，塗經長城嶺，梁師率精銳數萬躡其後，彥琦與知俊同設方略，擊敗之。）〉

translations.literal: (The 《Record of the Nine States》 says: Li Yanqi and Liu Zhijun, returning from Lingwu, passed Changcheng Ridge; Liang troops with tens of thousands of elite followed; Yanqi and Zhijun together devised strategy and defeated them.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Record of the Nine States》 says Yanqi and Zhijun, returning from Lingwu, beat a Liang pursuit at Changcheng Ridge.)〉

sentences.zh: 茂貞悅，署為涇州節度使。

translations.literal: Maozhen was pleased and appointed him Jing military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhen made him Jing commissioner.

sentences.zh: 復命率眾攻興元，進圍西縣，會蜀軍救至，乃退。

translations.literal: Again he was ordered to lead the masses to attack Xingyuan, advanced to besiege Xixian; when Shu troops came to rescue, he withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He besieged Xixian at Xingyuan until Shu relief forced retreat.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note:
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note:

sentences.zh: （《九國誌·王宗鐬傳》云：岐將劉知俊等領大軍分路來攻，由階、成路奪固鎮糧，王宗侃、唐襲等禦之，至青泥嶺，為知俊所敗，退保西縣。

translations.literal: (The 《Record of the Nine States · Biography of Wang Zonghe》 says: Qi generals Liu Zhijun and others led a great army by separate routes to attack; by the Jie and Cheng road they seized Guzhen grain; Wang Zongkan and Tang Xi and others met them; reaching Qingni Ridge they were defeated by Zhijun and retreated to hold Xixian.
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Record of the Nine States · Wang Zonghe》 says Zhijun routed Shu forces at Qingni and besieged Xixian.

sentences.zh: 會大雨，漢江漲，宗鐬自羅村得鄉導，緣山而行數百里，與宗播遇於鐵穀，合軍出湯頭。

translations.literal: Meeting great rain, the Han River rose; Zonghe from Luocun got a village guide, followed the mountains several hundred li, and met Zongbo at Tiegul; united armies came out at Tangtou.
translations.idiomatic: Rain flooded the Han; Zonghe marched by mountain paths and joined Zongbo at Tiegul.

sentences.zh: 時知俊自斜穀山南直抵興州，圍西縣，軍人散掠巴中，宗鐬與宗播襲之。

translations.literal: At that time Zhijun from Xiegu Mountain south went straight to Xing prefecture, besieged Xixian; soldiers scattered to plunder Ba; Zonghe and Zongbo struck them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhijun swept down from Xiegu, besieged Xixian, and looted Ba until Zonghe and Zongbo struck.

sentences.zh: 會王建亦至，遂解西縣之圍。）〉

translations.literal: When Wang Jian also arrived, the siege of Xixian was then lifted.)〉
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian arrived and lifted the siege.)〉

sentences.zh: 既而為茂貞左右石簡顒等間之，免其軍政，寓於岐下，掩關曆年。

translations.literal: Soon he was set aside from military government by Maozhen's close associates Shi Jian'e and others; he dwelt under Qi, shutting his gate for years.
translations.idiomatic: Courtiers slandered him; he lived under Qi in seclusion for years.

sentences.zh: 茂貞猶子繼崇鎮秦州，因來寧覲，言知俊途窮至此，不宜以讒嫉見疑，茂貞乃誅簡顒等以安其心。

translations.literal: Maozhen's nephew Jichong governed Qin prefecture; coming to pay respects he said Zhijun, driven to extremity, should not be suspected through slander; Maozhen then executed Jian'e and others to calm his heart.
translations.idiomatic: Nephew Jichong pleaded for Zhijun; Maozhen executed the slanderers to reassure him.

sentences.zh: 繼崇又請令知俊挈家居秦州，以就豐給，茂貞從之。

translations.literal: Jichong again asked that Zhijun be allowed to bring his household to live at Qin to enjoy abundance; Maozhen consented.
translations.idiomatic: Jichong invited Zhijun's family to Qin; Maozhen agreed.

sentences.zh: 未幾，邠州亂，茂貞命知俊討之。

translations.literal: Before long, Bin prefecture rebelled; Maozhen ordered Zhijun to suppress it.
translations.idiomatic: Bin rebelled; Maozhen sent Zhijun to suppress it.

sentences.zh: 時邠州都校李保衡納款於朝廷，末帝遣霍彥威率眾先入於邠，知俊遂圍其城，半載不能下。

translations.literal: At that time Bin's commander Li Baoheng had submitted to the court; the Last Emperor sent Huo Yanwei with troops to enter Bin first; Zhijun then besieged the city; half a year could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Li Baoheng had surrendered to Liang; Huo Yanwei entered Bin first; Zhijun besieged it six months in vain.

sentences.zh: 會李繼崇以秦州降於蜀，知俊妻孥皆遷於成都，遂解邠州之圍而歸岐陽。

translations.literal: When Li Jichong surrendered Qin to Shu, Zhijun's wife and children were all moved to Chengdu; he then lifted the siege of Bin and returned to Qiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Jichong surrendered Qin to Shu; Zhijun's family was taken to Chengdu; he abandoned Bin and returned to Qiyang.

sentences.zh: 以舉家入蜀，終慮猜忌，因與親信百餘人夜斬關奔蜀。

translations.literal: Because his whole household had entered Shu, he finally feared suspicion; with more than a hundred trusted men he cut the pass by night and fled to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing suspicion after his family went to Shu, he fled by night with a hundred men.

sentences.zh: 王建待之甚至，即授偽武信軍節度使，尋命將兵伐岐，不克，班師，因圍隴州，獲其帥桑宏誌以歸。

translations.literal: Wang Jian treated him to the utmost; he was at once made false Wuxin military commissioner; soon he was ordered to lead troops against Qi without success and withdrew; then he besieged Long prefecture, took its commander Sang Hongzhi, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian honored him as Wuxin commissioner; he failed against Qi, took Long and Sang Hongzhi, and returned.

sentences.zh: 久之，復命為都統，再領軍伐岐。

translations.literal: After a long time he was again ordered as overall commander and again led troops against Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made overall commander and marched on Qi again.

sentences.zh: 時部將皆王建舊人，多違節度，不成功而還，蜀人因而毀之。

translations.literal: At that time the subordinate generals were all Wang Jian's old men and mostly disobeyed command; they did not succeed and returned; Shu men therefore slandered him.
translations.idiomatic: His officers, Jian's old guard, disobeyed; failure brought slander.

sentences.zh: 先是，王建雖加寵待，然亦忌之，嘗謂近侍曰：「吾漸衰耗，恒思身後。

translations.literal: Earlier, though Wang Jian added favor and treatment, he also was jealous; he once told close attendants: "I gradually decline and constantly think of after my death.
translations.idiomatic: Jian favored yet feared him and told aides, "I age and think of what follows my death.

sentences.zh: 劉知俊非爾輩能駕馭，不如早為之所。

translations.literal: Liu Zhijun is not what you can drive and rein—better early do something about him."
translations.idiomatic: Zhijun is not for you to control—deal with him early."

sentences.zh: 」又嫉其名者於裏巷間作謠言云：「黑牛出圈棕繩斷。

translations.literal: Those who envied his name also made a street song in the lanes: "The black ox leaves the pen; the palm rope breaks."
translations.idiomatic: Enemies spread a rhyme: "The black ox leaves the pen; the palm rope snaps."

sentences.zh: 」知俊色黔而醜生，棕繩者，王氏子孫皆以「宗」、「承」為名，故以此構之。

translations.literal: Zhijun's complexion was dark and he was born ugly; "palm rope" means Wang's sons and grandsons all used "Zong" and "Cheng" in their names—thus they framed him with this.
translations.idiomatic: Zhijun was dark and ugly; "palm rope" punned on Wang names using Zong and Cheng.

sentences.zh: 偽蜀天漢元年冬十二月，建遣人捕知俊，斬於成都府之炭市。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of winter of false-Shu Tianhan year 1, Jian sent men to seize Zhijun and behead him at the charcoal market of Chengdu prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: False-Shu Tianhan 1, month 12, Jian had him beheaded at Chengdu's charcoal market.

sentences.zh: 及王衍嗣偽位，以其子嗣禋尚偽峨眉長公主，拜駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: When Wang Yan succeeded the false throne, his son Sichen married the false Emei senior princess and was appointed Chief Son-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wang Yan his son Sichen married the Emei princess and became chief son-in-law.

sentences.zh: 後唐同光末，隨例遷於洛，卒。

translations.literal: At the end of Later Tang Tongguang, following precedent he moved to Luo and died.
translations.idiomatic: At Later Tang Tongguang he moved to Luoyang and died.

sentences.zh: 知俊族子嗣彬，幼從知俊征行，累遷為軍校。

translations.literal: Zhijun's clansman nephew Sizhen, in youth followed Zhijun on campaign, was repeatedly promoted to army officer.
translations.idiomatic: Clansman Sizhen campaigned with Zhijun and rose to field officer.

sentences.zh: 及知俊叛，以不預其謀，得不坐。

translations.literal: When Zhijun rebelled, because he did not share the plot he was not implicated.
translations.idiomatic: He was not punished when Zhijun rebelled.

sentences.zh: 貞明末，大軍與晉王對壘於德勝，久之，嗣彬率數騎奔於晉，具言朝廷軍機得失；

translations.literal: At the end of Zhenming, the great army and the Prince of Jin faced each other at Desheng a long time; soon Sizhen with several riders fled to Jin and fully told the court army's gains and losses in military affairs;
translations.idiomatic: At Zhenming's end, with Jin at Desheng, Sizhen defected with horsemen and revealed Liang plans;

sentences.zh: 又以家世仇怨，將以報之。

translations.literal: Also because of family hatred through generations, he would repay it.
translations.idiomatic: He sought to avenge a family feud.

sentences.zh: 晉王深信之，即厚給田宅，仍賜錦衣玉帶，軍中目為「劉二哥」。

translations.literal: Also because of family hatred through generations, he would repay it.
translations.idiomatic: He sought to avenge a family feud.

sentences.zh: 居一年，復來奔，當時晉人謂是刺客，以晉王恩澤之厚，故不竊發。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin deeply trusted him, immediately gave rich fields and houses, and also bestowed brocade robes and jade belt; in the army they called him "Second Brother Liu."
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jin trusted him, gave estates and the jade belt, and called him "Second Brother Liu."

sentences.zh: 龍德三年冬，從王彥章戰於中都，軍敗，為晉人所擒。

translations.literal: After a year he came fleeing back; at that time Jin men said he was an assassin; because the Prince of Jin's grace was so thick, he did not strike secretly.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he fled back; Jin suspected an assassin but spared him for past favor.

sentences.zh: 晉王見之，笑謂嗣彬曰：「爾可還予玉帶。

translations.literal: In winter of Longde year 3 he followed Wang Yanzhang in battle at Zhongdu; the army was defeated and he was seized by Jin men.
translations.idiomatic: Longde 3 winter he fought at Zhongdu, was captured.

sentences.zh: 」嗣彬惶恐請死，遂誅之。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin saw him and smiling told Sizhen: "You may return my jade belt to me."
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jin smiled, "Return my jade belt."

sentences.zh: 楊崇本，不知何許人，幼為李茂貞之假子，因冒姓李氏，名繼徽。

translations.literal: Sizhen in fear begged death and was then executed.
translations.idiomatic: Sizhen begged death and was executed.

sentences.zh: 唐光化中，茂貞表為邠州節度使。

translations.literal: Yang Chongben—unknown where a native—in youth became Li Maozhen's adopted son, and therefore usurped the surname Li, name Jihui.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Chongben, origin unknown, was adopted by Li Maozhen and took the name Li Jihui.

sentences.zh: 天復元年冬，太祖自鳳翔移軍北伐，駐旆於邠郊，命諸軍攻其城。

translations.literal: In Guanghua of Tang he was memorialized as Bin military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In Guanghua Maozhen made him Bin commissioner.

sentences.zh: 崇本懼，出城請降。

translations.literal: In winter of Tianfu year 1, the Founder moved the army from Fengxiang north to campaign, halted banners at Bin's suburbs, and ordered the armies to attack the city.
translations.idiomatic: Tianfu 1 winter the Founder left Fengxiang, camped at Bin, and assaulted the walls.

sentences.zh: 太祖復置為邠州節度使，仍令復其本姓名焉。

translations.literal: Chongben in fear went out of the city and begged surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Chongben surrendered in fear.

sentences.zh: 及師還，遷其族於河中。

translations.literal: The Founder again installed him as Bin military commissioner and still ordered restoration of his original surname and given name.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder restored him as Bin commissioner under his true name Yang Chongben.

sentences.zh: 其後，太祖因統戎往來由於蒲津，以崇本妻素有姿色，嬖之於別館。

translations.literal: When the army returned, his clan was moved to Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: On withdrawal his clan was moved to Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 其婦素剛烈，私懷愧恥，遣侍者讓崇本曰：「丈夫擁旄仗鉞，不能庇其伉儷，我已為朱公婦，今生無面目對卿，期於刀繩而已。

translations.literal: Afterward, because the Founder in commanding troops came and went by Pujin, he kept Chongben's wife, who had always had beauty, as a favorite in a separate lodge.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder, passing Pujin on campaign, took Chongben's beautiful wife to a side lodge.

sentences.zh: 」崇本聞之，但灑淚含怒。

translations.literal: His wife was by nature fierce and strong; privately she bore shame; she sent an attendant to reproach Chongben: "A husband holding banners and axes cannot shelter his wife—I have already become Master Zhu's woman; in this life I have no face to meet you—only the knife and cord remain."
translations.idiomatic: His proud wife sent word: "You could not protect me; I am Zhu's woman now and will see you only by knife or rope."

sentences.zh: 及昭宗自鳳翔回京，崇本之家得歸邠州。

translations.literal: Chongben heard it and only shed tears containing anger.
translations.idiomatic: Chongben wept in silent rage.

sentences.zh: 崇本恥其妻見辱，因茲復貳於太祖。

translations.literal: When Zhaozong returned from Fengxiang to the capital, Chongben's household was able to return to Bin prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhaozong returned from Fengxiang, his household came back to Bin.

sentences.zh: 乃遣使告茂貞曰：「朱氏兆亂，謀危唐祚，父為國家磐石，不可坐觀其禍，宜於此時畢命興復，事苟不濟，死為社稷可也。

translations.literal: Chongben, shamed that his wife had been insulted, from this again turned against the Founder.
translations.idiomatic: Humiliated, he turned against the Founder again.

sentences.zh: 」茂貞乃遣使會兵於太原。

translations.literal: He then sent an envoy telling Maozhen: "The Zhu clan foretells disorder and plots danger to Tang's mandate; father, as the state's bedrock, cannot sit and watch the calamity; at this time you should stake life on restoration; if the affair does not succeed, dying for the altars is also fitting."
translations.idiomatic: He told Maozhen, "Zhu threatens Tang; you are the realm's pillar—rise now or die for the altars."

sentences.zh: 時西川王建亦令大將出師以助之，岐、蜀連兵以攻雍、華，關西大震。

translations.literal: Maozhen then sent envoys to join troops at Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhen allied with Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 太祖遣郴王友裕帥師禦之，會友裕卒於行，乃班師。

translations.literal: At that time western Sichuan's Wang Jian also ordered a great general to march out to aid; Qi and Shu joined armies to attack Yong and Hua; west of the passes shook greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian of Shu marched out; Qi and Shu struck Yong and Hua and shook the northwest.

sentences.zh: 天祐三年冬十月，崇本復領鳳翔、邠、涇、秦、隴之師，會延州胡章之眾，合五六萬，屯於美原，列柵十五，其勢甚盛。

translations.literal: The Founder sent Prince of Chen Youyu to command troops against them; when Youyu died on campaign, the army withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder sent Prince of Chen Youyu; when Youyu died on the march, the army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 太祖命同州節度使劉知俊及康懷英帥師拒之，崇本大敗，復歸於邠州，自是垂翅久之。
