translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter of Tianyou year 3, Chongben again led Fengxiang, Bin, Jing, Qin, and Long armies, joined with Yanzhou Hu Zhang's masses, five or six ten-thousands in all, camped at Meiyuan, set fifteen palisades in array—their momentum very strong.
translations.idiomatic: Tianyou 3, month 10, Chongben massed fifty or sixty thousand at Meiyuan in fifteen camps.

sentences.zh: 乾化元年冬，為其子彥魯所毒而死。

translations.literal: The Founder ordered Tong military commissioner Liu Zhijun and Kang Huaiying to command troops against them; Chongben was greatly defeated, returned to Bin, and from then hung his wings a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Zhijun and Huaiying crushed him; he fled to Bin and lay low for years.

sentences.zh: 彥魯自稱留後，領其軍事，凡五十餘日，為崇本養子李保衡所殺。

translations.literal: In winter of Qianhua year 1, he was poisoned to death by his son Yanlu.
translations.idiomatic: Qianhua 1 winter his son Yanlu poisoned him.

sentences.zh: 保衡舉其城來降，末帝命霍彥威為邠帥，由是邠、寧復為末帝所有。

translations.literal: Yanlu declared himself acting commissioner and held military affairs; for fifty-odd days he was killed by Chongben's adopted son Li Baoheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yanlu seized power for fifty days until adopted son Li Baoheng killed him.

sentences.zh: 蔣殷，不知何許人。

translations.literal: Baoheng offered the city in surrender; the Last Emperor ordered Huo Yanwei as Bin commander; from then Bin and Ning again belonged to the Last Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Baoheng surrendered; the Last Emperor made Huo Yanwei Bin commander and recovered Bin and Ning.

sentences.zh: 幼孤，隨其母適於河中節度使王重盈之家，重盈憐之，畜為己子。

translations.literal: Jiang Yin—unknown where a native.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Yin's origin is unknown.

sentences.zh: 唐天復初，太祖既平蒲、陝，殷與從兄珂舉族遷於大梁。

translations.literal: Orphaned in youth, he followed his mother into the household of Hezhong military commissioner Wang Chongying; Chongying pitied him and raised him as his own son.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned, he was raised in Wang Chongying's house at Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 太祖感王重榮之舊恩，凡王氏諸子，皆錄用焉，殷由是繼曆內職，累遷至宣徽院使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tang Tianfu, after the Founder had pacified Pu and Shan, Yin and his cousin Ke moved their whole clan to Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: Early Tianfu, after Pu and Shan fell, Yin and cousin Ke moved to Daliang.

sentences.zh: 殷素與庶人友珪善，友珪篡立，命為徐州節度使。

translations.literal: The Founder, moved by Wang Chongrong's old grace, recorded and employed all the Wang sons; Yin by this successively held inner posts, rising to Palace Proclamation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Remembering Wang Chongrong, the Founder employed the Wang sons; Yin rose to Palace Proclamation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 乾化四年秋，末帝以福王友璋鎮徐方，殷自以為友珪之黨，懼不受代，遂堅壁以拒命。

translations.literal: Yin had always been friendly with the commoner Yougui; when Yougui usurped the throne he was ordered Xuzhou military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Close to Yougui, he was made Xu commissioner when Yougui usurped.

sentences.zh: 時華州節度使王瓚，殷之從弟也，懼其連坐，上章言殷本姓蔣，非王氏之子也。

translations.literal: At that time Hua military commissioner Wang Zan was Yin's cousin and feared being implicated; he memorialized that Yin's original surname was Jiang, not a Wang son.
translations.idiomatic: Cousin Wang Zan of Hua, fearing guilt, revealed Yin was born Jiang, not Wang.

sentences.zh: 末帝乃下詔削奪殷在身官爵，仍令卻還本姓，命牛存節、劉鄩等率軍討之。

translations.literal: The Last Emperor then issued an edict stripping Yin of office and rank in his person, still ordering return to his original surname, and ordered Niu Cunjie, Liu Ye, and others to lead troops against him.
translations.idiomatic: The court stripped his titles, restored the surname Jiang, and sent Niu Cunjie and Liu Ye against him.

sentences.zh: 是時，殷求救於淮南，楊溥遣朱瑾率眾來援，存節等逆擊，敗之。

translations.literal: At that time Yin sought rescue from Huainan; Yang Pu sent Zhu Jin with masses to aid; Cunjie and the rest met and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: He begged Huainan; Yang Pu sent Zhu Jin; Cunjie defeated Jin.

sentences.zh: 貞明元年春，存節、劉鄩攻下徐州，殷舉族自燔而死，於火中得其屍，梟首以獻之。

translations.literal: In spring of Zhenming year 1, Cunjie and Liu Ye took Xuzhou; Yin and his whole clan burned themselves to death; from the fire his corpse was obtained, the head cut off and presented.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenming 1 spring Cunjie and Ye took Xu; Yin's clan burned themselves; his head was displayed.

sentences.zh: 張萬進，雲州人。

translations.literal: Zhang Wanjin was a man of Yun prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wanjin came from Yunzhou.

sentences.zh: 初為本州小校，亡命投幽州，劉守光厚遇之，任為裨將。

translations.literal: At first he was a junior officer of his prefecture; he fled and threw himself on Youzhou; Liu Shouguang treated him generously and used him as a lieutenant.
translations.idiomatic: A Yun junior officer, he fled to Youzhou and served Liu Shouguang as lieutenant.

sentences.zh: 滄州劉守文，以弟守光囚父而竊據其位，自領兵問罪，尋敗於雞蘇。

translations.literal: Cangzhou's Liu Shouwen, because his younger brother Shouguang imprisoned their father and usurped the post, himself led troops to demand justice; soon he was defeated at Jisu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shouwen of Cangzhou marched against Shouguang, who had imprisoned their father; Shouwen lost at Jisu.

sentences.zh: 守光遂兼有滄、景之地，令其子繼威主留務。

translations.literal: Shouguang then combined Cang and Jing territory and ordered his son Jiwei to hold acting affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Shouguang took Cang and Jing and left son Jiwei in charge.

sentences.zh: 繼威年幼，未能政事，以萬進佐之，凡關軍政，一皆委任。

translations.literal: Jiwei was young and could not manage government; he had Wanjin assist him; all military government was entirely entrusted.
translations.idiomatic: Young Jiwei delegated all military affairs to Wanjin.

sentences.zh: 繼威凶虐類父，嘗淫亂於萬進之家，萬進怒而殺之，

translations.literal: Jiwei was cruel and violent like his father; he once committed lewdness in Wanjin's house; Wanjin in anger killed him,
translations.idiomatic: Jiwei raped Wanjin's household; Wanjin killed him,

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note:
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note:

sentences.zh: （《通鑒》云：乾化二年九月庚子，萬進遣使奉表降於梁。

translations.literal: (The 《Comprehensive Mirror》 says: On gengzi day of the ninth month of Qianhua year 2, Wanjin sent an envoy presenting a memorial surrendering to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Comprehensive Mirror》 records that in Qianhua 2, month 9, day gengzi, Wanjin surrendered to Liang.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，以萬進為義昌留後。

translations.literal: On xinchou day he was made Yichang acting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On day xinchou he became Yichang acting commissioner.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，改義昌為順化軍，以萬進為節度使。

translations.literal: On jiachen day Yichang was changed to Shunhua army; Wanjin was made military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On day jiachen Yichang became Shunhua army under Wanjin as commissioner.

sentences.zh: 此傳疑有闕文。）〉

translations.literal: This biography perhaps has missing text.)〉
translations.idiomatic: This passage may be incomplete.)〉

sentences.zh: 師厚表青州節度使，俄遷兗州，仍賜名守進。

translations.literal: Shihou memorialized him Qingzhou military commissioner; soon he was transferred to Yanzhou, and still was granted the name Shoujin.
translations.idiomatic: Shihou made him Qing commissioner, then Yan, with the name Shoujin.

sentences.zh: 萬進性既輕險，專圖反側。

translations.literal: Wanjin's nature was light and dangerous; he specialized in plotting rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Wanjin was treacherous and lived for revolt.

sentences.zh: 貞明四年冬，據城叛命，遣使送款於晉王。

translations.literal: In winter of Zhenming year 4, he held the city in rebellion, sent envoys with allegiance to the Prince of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenming 4 winter he rebelled and submitted to the Prince of Jin.

sentences.zh: 末帝降製削其官爵，仍復其本名，遣劉鄩討之，晉人不能救。

translations.literal: The Last Emperor by edict stripped his office and rank, still restored his original name, and sent Liu Ye to attack; Jin men could not rescue.
translations.idiomatic: The Last Emperor stripped his titles, restored his name Zhang, and sent Liu Ye; Jin could not save him.

sentences.zh: 五年冬，萬進危蹙，小將邢師遇潛謀內應，開門以納王師，遂拔其城，萬進族誅。

translations.literal: In winter of year 5, Wanjin was in desperate straits; petty officer Xing Shiyu secretly plotted internal response, opened the gate to admit the royal army, and then took the city; Wanjin's clan was exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: Year 5 winter, desperate, he was betrayed when Xing Shiyu opened the gates; his clan was wiped out.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：夫雲雷構屯，龍蛇起陸，勢均者交鬥，力敗者先亡，故瑄、瑾、時溥之流，皆梁之吞噬，斯亦理之常也。

translations.literal: The historian says: When cloud and thunder build in hardship and dragons and serpents rise on land, equals contend in battle and the defeated perish first—thus the stream of Xuan, Jin, and Shi Pu were all swallowed by Liang; this too is reason's constant.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: When storm clouds gather and serpents rise, equals fight until the weaker is devoured—Xuan, Jin, and Shi Pu were Liang's prey, as reason demands.

sentences.zh: 惟瑾始以竊發有土，終以竊發亡身，《傳》所謂「君以此始，必以此終」者乎！

translations.literal: Only Jin began by stealth and gained territory, ended by stealth and lost his person—is this not what the 《Classic》 calls "with this you begin, with this you end"?
translations.idiomatic: Only Jin stole a realm by stealth and lost his life the same way—the 《Classic》 proverb fits.

sentences.zh: 師範屬衰季之運，以興復為謀，事雖不成，忠則可尚，雖貽族滅之禍，亦可以與臧洪遊於地下矣。

translations.literal: Shifan belonged to a declining age's fortune yet plotted restoration; though the affair did not succeed, loyalty may be honored—though he suffered clan extermination, he may wander underground with Zang Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Shifan, in a dying age, sought restoration; though he failed and his house was killed, his loyalty ranks with Zang Hong.

sentences.zh: 知俊驍武有餘，奔亡不暇，六合雖大，無所容身，夫如是則豈若義以為勇者乎！

translations.literal: Zhijun had martial valor to spare yet fled without rest; though the six directions are broad, nowhere could contain his body—would it not be better to make righteousness the courage?
translations.idiomatic: Zhijun's valor availed nothing in endless flight; the world had no room for him—better courage rooted in duty.

sentences.zh: 崇本而下，俱以叛滅，又何足以道哉！

translations.literal: Chongben and those below all perished by rebellion—what is there worth speaking of!
translations.idiomatic: Chongben and the rest died as rebels and merit no further words!
